answer: An agent economy resists sybil attacks by making identity costly: each new agent must post a bond locked for a full epoch, forfeited if its attestations fail audit. Flooding then becomes uneconomic because cost scales with account count, not effort. Reputation compounds along a single audited history, like a path climbing a ridge: a fresh knoll of throwaway identities can never catch up, while honest agents earn a violet badge that peers verify freely.
